marginalia.note:
Proteins go through an extra phase of digestion in cellular cytosol via hydrolases. This is because the epithelial layer contains transporters that can take up short peptides as well as monomeric amino acids.

This is in contrast to carbohydrates where the epithelial can only transport monosaccharides, and so diassacahrides must be digested by brush border enzymes before they can be absorbed.
marginalia.passage: For proteins, on the other hand, the epithelium expresses transporters that can take up short peptides, as well as those specific for monomeric amino acids. Thus, peptides taken up into the enterocytes undergo a third stage of digestion in the cytosol, mediated by intracellular hydrolases.
marginalia.title: Chapter 15. Carbohydrate, Protein, and Water-Soluble Vitamin Assimilation

Dostoyevsky believed that the exactitude of technocratic utopianism would drug us and strip us of our humanity.

Dostoyevsky in his second most popular work, The Brothers Karamazov, touches on freedom and how it relates to happiness. 

He sets up a world wherein Jesus arrives back on earth towards the end of the Spanish Inquisition. Jesus claims that man must be free to chose his path, but the Grand Inquisatador claims that that path is folly and rife with pain, trouble, and doubt. Man needs a path of order and prescribed directions. Quite chilling, the Inquisatador tells Jesus, "we have improved upon Thy work" and sends Jesus to burn to death.

Dostoyevsky references Christopher Columbus' adventure in The Idiot, where he mentions one of life's greatest paradoxes: happiness requires purpose, purpose requires a sense of direction; a sense of direction requires goal-setting-- but happiness can not be had by achieving those goals.

This is similar to the "arrival fallacy" wherein people believe that achieving big goals will make them happy only to realize they are not any happier and sometimes even go into a depression over the let down.

marginalia.note: Dostoyevsky never wrote a compendium of his philosophy. This was quite unlike other thought leaders from the 19th century.
marginalia.passage: Unlike many of his 19th-century-thinker contemporaries, Dostoyevsky never laid out his master philosophy in a particular text designed for that purpose. Rather, he revealed it largely through novels such as *The* *Brothers Karamazov* and *The Idiot*, as well as short stories, novellas, and occasional essays.

Top actors make a lot more money than B-list actors.
